title: Envelope accepts noncontributory X25519 recipients
reproduction: Run the bounded Envelope recipient conformance harness against the committed WASM. Encode synthetic u=0 and u=1 as correctly checksummed agreement-public-key URs; call recipient-only protected creation with public entropy and TREZOR.
expected: Reject a recipient that produces an all-zero X25519 shared secret before returning any protected record. Preserve correct recipient and SSKR recovery.
observed: Both rejection assertions fail: protected records are returned. Independent Noble X25519 controls refuse both points. Two ordinary recipient private keys and a two-of-three SSKR quorum recover exact entropy and TREZOR; a wrong key/no permit refuse.
impact: The pinned bc-crypto path feeds the shared secret into HKDF without rejecting zero. For these points, the recipient wrapping key is therefore determined by public constants, so recipient-only confidentiality cannot be relied on; adding another permit does not repair a weak permit. This impact follows from the bound source path and cryptographic semantics. Independent decryption without a private key was not executed. Ordinary generated recipient keys were not shown defective.
recommendedFix: Place one contributory-recipient admission rule in the Rust protection owner, enforce it for every recipient before content-key wrapping, and propagate a clear refusal through all bindings. Prefer checked fallible encapsulation returning an error on the actual all-zero shared secret, including noncanonical equivalent encodings; do not duplicate a page-only blacklist.
requiredVerification: Actual compiled WASM refusal of low-order and equivalent encodings plus ordinary recipient/SSKR controls; library proof that all-zero agreement cannot yield a wrapping key. Canonical source/output verification at release.
qualification: RFC 7748 allows an all-zero check; it does not impose universal syntactic rejection. The finding concerns the application's confidential recipient permit, not noncompliance with a mandatory RFC parsing rule.

title: Codex32 zero-padded random basis reveals a secret bit below threshold
reproduction: Enumerate the two final-byte low-bit choices of the random basis for a synthetic 32-byte two-of-two share set, twice for secrets differing only in their final bit. Inspect the final payload symbol of index c and retain exact two-share restoration controls.
expected: The distribution of a below-threshold share must not identify a bit of the secret. Random basis elements must cover the full GF(32) payload symbol space, including padding positions.
observed: The last-symbol supports are disjoint: secret bit0 gives p/q and bit1 gives 3/s. All four two-share round-trip controls restore exact inputs. from_seed supplies zero padding for the last four bits of both the master and the random basis.
impact: For this supported 256-bit two-of-two layout, one index-c share identifies the secret's last bit. This is a one-bit threshold secrecy violation, not recovery of an entire mnemonic or demonstrated fund loss. The fixture enumerates the last-symbol projection; pointwise GF(32) interpolation makes other payload symbols irrelevant to that projection. No large statistical run was used.
recommendedFix: Generate random basis records with independent uniform GF(32) symbols including padding positions, using one validated reference-implementation entry point. Keep canonical master data encoding, valid BIP93 checksums and interoperability.
requiredVerification: Independent finite-field projection check and below-threshold secrecy cases at every non-byte-aligned supported length, including other thresholds/indexes; known BIP93 values and reconstruction/refusal tests.

title: Codex32 restoration rejects compatible records in different presentation cases
reproduction: Use official BIP93 shared vector two. Restore both full-uppercase records, both full-lowercase records, then one uppercase and one lowercase record.
expected: Each individually valid presentation case denotes the same data and compatible shares restore the pinned seed. Mixed case within one record remains invalid.
observed: Both uniform-case controls restore d1808e096b35b209ca12132b264662a5; the compatible cross-record case pair fails with incompatible prefixes. A within-record mixed-case control correctly refuses.
impact: A valid backup can be rejected after one complete record is transcribed in the other permitted case. Manual whole-record case normalization is a workaround.
recommendedFix: Validate each original record for its case/checksum rules, then normalize admitted semantic prefixes before interpolation. Correct the test that conflates cross-record presentation differences with mixed case within a record.
requiredVerification: Published upper/lower/cross-record combinations plus mixed-within-record, wrong HRP, checksum, identity, threshold and duplicate-index refusals.

title: Envelope restoration discards malformed or ambiguous passphrase assertions
reproduction: Pass small correctly typed synthetic Seed Envelope records with a string passphrase, no passphrase, a numeric passphrase object and two distinct string passphrase assertions to the actual committed bundle-recovery WASM.
expected: Absent is distinct from malformed or ambiguous. Restore valid string values; refuse wrong types and duplicate conflicting assertions instead of substituting an empty BIP39 passphrase.
observed: Valid TREZOR and absent controls pass. Both wrong-type and duplicate rejection assertions fail. Rust extract_object_for_predicate(...).ok() converts all extraction errors to None and the JS bundle omits the field.
impact: An accepted record can silently select the entropy-only wallet rather than the intended phrase-plus-passphrase wallet. This affects malformed/imported containers; ordinary well-formed generated controls preserved their passphrase. No external container, real wallet or loss was used.
recommendedFix: Use the library's optional typed extraction contract to distinguish a genuinely absent predicate from extraction failure. Propagate wrong-type/ambiguity errors and preserve valid empty/string semantics through bundle handoff.
requiredVerification: Actual WASM absent/empty/nonempty/wrong-type/duplicate bundle controls and host handoff; encrypted recipient and SSKR recovery preserve exact entropy and passphrase.

title: Dash Shielded derivation wipes the caller seed and changes output on reuse
reproduction: Call actual deriveDashShielded with one synthetic 64-byte seed and one testnet address. Inspect caller bytes, call again with the same buffer, and compare with a fresh copy of the original seed.
expected: The derivation API borrows caller seed data. Owned copies are wiped without changing future derivation from the same caller input.
observed: The first call zeros the caller buffer. Reuse produces a different address/spending key; a fresh original-seed copy reproduces the first output. Rust mut slice zeroization is copied back by wasm-bindgen glue.
impact: API composition or caller reuse can derive the all-zero-seed wallet after the first call. No UI loss or actual funded output was demonstrated; ordinary callers that supply a disposable copy may avoid the effect.
recommendedFix: Give the WASM boundary an explicit owned copy and wipe it on all paths; keep the caller buffer intact. Retain zeroization of WASM-owned secret memory and document ownership consistently.
requiredVerification: Actual WASM success/failure paths preserve caller bytes; repeated calls and mixed protocol derivations remain deterministic; fresh-copy control and independent pinned Orchard output remain valid.
